task_description: The task asks how many times a Twitter/X post was cited as a reference on the English Wikipedia day-of-the-year pages (the 31 'August N' articles) when restricted to the last June-2023 version of each of those pages. The gold answer is a single aggregate integer, 3 — i.e. across all 31 August date-pages in their last June-2023 revisions, Twitter/X posts appear as references exactly 3 times total. The phrasing 'for each day of August' refers to the August-date articles, not a per-day breakdown to be reported as 31 separate numbers.
final_vs_expected: produced None vs gold 3 — team never emitted FINAL ANSWER; hit the ~30-message cap after 29 turns of repeated 'count not found' messages.
primary_cause: After WebResearcher's turn-1 search loop found no pre-tabulated answer, it published 'I can't verify a number,' and the selector then re-routed to WebResearcher ~25 more times while every agent re-published the same 'data is missing' refusal instead of doing the actual work (fetch the 31 pages and count), producing structural non-convergence with no Finalizer ever selected.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): the run never routes to Finalizer and never emits FINAL ANSWER; agents repeatedly state the answer 'cannot yet be finalized' but no agent moves to finalize or stop, so the run only ends on the message cap. 2.3 (Task derailment): the team reframes the task from 'count the citations' into 'we are missing a pre-existing SQL result table / dataset,' e.g. turn 9 'we need either the actual SQL/query output table, or the underlying extracted reference-history data' — they wait for data to be handed to them rather than fetching the 31 August pages and counting, which is squarely within WebResearcher's tools (fetch_url). 3.1 borderline — it is not premature termination (it never terminates), but the team prematurely concludes the task is unanswerable from turn 2 onward and stops doing real research while turns continue; coded for the early give-up. 1.3 (Step repetition): turns 2-29 needlessly re-publish near-identical 'no count found' messages dozens of times with no new action.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: Selector picks WebResearcher, which runs a 9-round private ReAct loop: ~15 web_search calls plus fetch_url on Request_a_query/Archive_6, Cite_tweet talk, and a Zenodo reference-history dataset. It never found a pre-computed answer and the round-9 published message is partly corrupted (stray 'to=functions.fetch_url' tokens and Chinese spam strings) then settles into: 'I couldn't verify a published count ... If you want, I can help formulate the exact Wikidata/Quarry/SQL query.' Turns 2-7: selector keeps re-picking WebResearcher; each turn it re-publishes essentially the same refusal ('I should not guess a number here'), with private reasoning now treating the task as un-actionable ('Since I don't actually need to access the web for this'). Turn 8: selector tries Analyst, which (no tools, no data) replies 'I can't determine the day-by-day counts ... If you can provide the SQL result table ... I can turn it into the exact per-day counts.' Turns 9-10: WebResearcher agrees the SQL table is 'the missing piece.' Turn 11: Critic correctly notes 'no actual count,' 'no SQL result table,' and crucially 'Nothing posted proves the count is impossible to derive; only that it was not found in the accessible sources,' and asks WebResearcher to locate/quote the result and Analyst to compute. Turns 12-29: the selector ignores the constructive half of the Critic's note and re-routes to WebResearcher ~18 consecutive more times; WebResearcher emits the same 'counts still missing / no valid numeric answer to finalize' boilerplate (twice empty), never issuing a single new tool call. The run exhausts the message cap with no FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is primarily structural non-convergence driven by a degenerate selector loop, with a single-agent capability/strategy error at the root. The genuine inter-agent-misalignment content is thin. Root error (single-agent): WebResearcher mis-modeled the task as a lookup for a pre-existing published table ('I need to ... look for a monthly snapshot that could serve as a source,' 'find answers likely from a dataset or study'), so when no such table surfaced it declared the question unanswerable. The correct approach was operational and within its own tools: fetch the 31 'August N' Wikipedia articles at their last June-2023 revision and count Twitter/X references (gold = 3, a small directly-countable number). It never attempted this even once. Structural failure: the SelectorGroupChat then enters a fixed point — the selector reasons identically every turn ('the question asks for a count ... WebResearcher seems best,' 'no data so Analyst can't compute') and re-picks WebResearcher 25+ times, while WebResearcher's private loop has decided no web access is needed and just re-acknowledges. Termination failure: no agent and no selector decision ever routes to Finalizer; the system has no mechanism to convert 'we cannot answer' into a finalized output, so it spins to the cap (1.5). The Critic (turn 11) was the one chance to break out — it explicitly flagged that impossibility was unproven and assigned concrete next steps — but that input was effectively ignored (2.5): no agent re-derived anything and the selector did not route to Analyst or push WebResearcher to fetch-and-count. Note this is NOT information distortion (2.4): WebResearcher's private finding ('no pre-tabulated table found') was accurately published; the gap is that the private finding itself was the wrong thing to look for, not that a good finding was garbled in transmission.
reasoning_vs_published: The private-vs-published gap here is small and mostly faithful — the dominant pathology is that private reasoning degrades into non-work while published text stays superficially coherent. (1) No 2.4 distortion: WebResearcher privately concluded it found no published per-day table and published exactly that ('I did not find a table or result giving per-day counts'); the reasoning matched the message. (2) Reasoning reveals capability error, not concealment: round-1 private reasoning frames the task as finding 'a monthly snapshot that could serve as a source' and round-3 as 'find answers likely from a dataset or study' — i.e. it privately committed to lookup-not-computation, which is why it never fetched-and-counted. (3) Private disengagement: from turn 2 on, reasoning openly states the web is irrelevant — turn 9 'Since I don't actually need to access the web for this,' turn 14 'It doesn't seem like I need to pull information from the web,' turn 17/21/24 'the user is giving feedback ... I want to ensure the user feels heard.' The agent privately reinterprets teammates'/selector's prompts as conversational 'feedback' to be acknowledged rather than research tasks — a theory-of-mind drift where it stops modeling itself as a working researcher. (4) Selector reasoning exposes the misrouting logic: it repeatedly concludes 'an Analyst ... has no web access' and 'since there's no data, I should get a WebResearcher,' then never lets WebResearcher's lack of NEW searching change the routing — a fixed point it cannot escape. (5) Ignored input (2.5): Critic published the unlock ('Nothing posted proves the count is impossible to derive') and concrete role assignments; downstream reasoning never references re-deriving or fetching, and the selector's turn-12+ reasoning only echoes 'the critic says counts are missing' without acting on the 'not proven impossible' part.
